title: Engine Ignition: Component Locations
introduction:
This drawing lays out the ignition components along the sloping cylinder banks, with the curved intake runners between them. I use those runners as a landmark, then follow the blue coil assemblies down toward the green spark-plug ends. Read the callouts through the table's Item and Description columns.

The coil and plug are partners with different jobs: the coil produces high voltage, and the plug gives that voltage a controlled gap across which to spark. The colorful cutaway saves a game of engine-bay hide-and-seek by making surrounding parts transparent. It shows component relationships, not a physical access procedure. Use separate engine-specific information for plug specifications, removal or fault testing.

edits.why: Confirm the complete engine label before applying the drawing. The callout leaders identify highlighted components on both banks, and the unchanged table supplies their names. The layout does not assign cylinder numbers or prove that an identified component is faulty.
